title: AKSHAR declaration-block ground truth
description: Per-image field labels for the declaration-block evaluation set. Describes data/declaration_blocks/ground_truth.json. Tracked in git although the images are not, so the shape and the content of the labels survive where the pixels do not, and a score reported against them can be re-derived.

note.description: The rule the whole file is annotated under. It matters more than any single label: the set records what is printed IN THIS FRAME, not what the product declares somewhere else on the pack, because the frame is what the extractor is handed.

field_mapping.description: How Rule 6(1)(a)'s name-and-address labels map onto contracts.FieldName. Written down because 'Marketed by' could defensibly be annotated as either manufacturer or packer, and a scorer comparing against a different choice would report an extraction error where there is only a vocabulary disagreement.

image.description: Filename under data/declaration_blocks/images/. Joins to manifest.json, which carries the SHA-256 of the bytes these labels were read from.

product.description: What the pack is, as identified from the panel itself rather than from the filename. Several delivered filenames name a different product from the one photographed; where they disagree the disagreement is recorded in notes, because a filename is not evidence.

fields.description: One entry per statutory declaration legible in this frame. A field absent from this object is absent from the frame. A field mapped to null is printed but carries no readable value here - a smudged overprint, or a cross-reference such as 'See on Crimp'. A field mapped to an array carries more than one distinct value on the same panel, which is Rule 6(3) material rather than an annotation error.

blank_labels.description: Declarations whose LABEL is printed on the pack with no value after it - an empty 'Batch No.', an empty 'Mfg & Consumer Cared By'. This is a non-compliance in the package, not a failure of extraction, and it is separated from `fields` so that no scoring run can ever count it as a miss. Nothing in the pipeline is asked to distinguish these; the distinction lives here so that a human reading a score knows which way an absence points.

notes.description: What makes this frame hard, in the terms the pipeline has to deal with: offset value columns, dot-matrix overprint, curvature, occlusion, reversed type. Written at annotation time rather than after seeing a result, so it cannot be an explanation invented to fit a failure.
